{% raw %}
`uptime`: tell how long the computer has been running.

## Synopsis

<strong>uptime</strong> \[<strong>-p</strong>\]

## Description

<strong>uptime</strong> prints how long the computer has been running since it booted, as procps's uptime does:

```text
 up 5 min
 up  1:05
 up 2 days,  1:05
```

## Options

<strong>-p</strong>, <strong>--pretty</strong>
: Says it in words: <strong>up 1 hour, 5 minutes</strong>.

## Exit status

0; 1, with a usage message, for any other argument.

## Notes

mcos has no real-time clock, so there is no time of day; and no load average or user count either. The uptime is the machine's own clock, which stands still while its chunk is unloaded.

## See also

<strong>ps</strong>(1), <strong>free</strong>(1), <strong>time</strong>(1)
